title: Always-on worker or activate-on-demand: which costs less for the same jobs?
hypothesis: An activate-on-trigger worker handles 20 jobs a day for under half the monthly cost of an always-on worker, with time to first action under 60 seconds.
human_gate: Frank approves the monthly Railway cap before any service is created.

arms.role: always-on, one worker polling for issues
activated by GitHub webhook or cron, sleeps when idle

suite: synthetic trigger load: 20 no-op jobs per day for 7 days
success_rule: Activated topology projected cost is under 50% of always-on and p50 trigger-to-first-action is under 60 seconds with zero missed jobs.
kill: Stop at $3 of Railway spend. If Railway cannot sleep a service or bill by use, record that and keep the always-on design with a single worker.

next_gate.receipt: lab/results/EXP-004.md with the Railway usage export and latency table

decision_it_feeds: The topology and monthly cap for the cloud worker fleet.

prior_evidence.claim: Railway sleep-when-idle behaviour and pricing have not been verified.
prior_evidence.caveat: That is why this experiment exists. Do not quote a Railway price until it has measured one.
